pages.title: The Pharaoh’s Fear
pages.content: Moses (pbuh) was a great prophet of Allah. He was born in the land of Egypt. He lived there in the 13th century BC, over 3000 years ago. At that time, the Pharaoh ruled Egypt. He was a dictatorial king of Egypt. He did not believe in Allah and saw himself as a god. The Children of Israel or the Israelites were a large group in Egypt. They were the children of Jacob (pbuh), who was also the father of Joseph (pbuh), and Prophet Abraham (pbuh) was their grandfather. They believed in Allah alone, just like their ancestor, Prophet Abraham (pbuh). So, they did not believe that the Pharaoh was a god. The Pharaoh feared that this group, which was larger than the Egyptians, would take control of his kingdom. That’s why he was rude and harsh to the Children of Israel. He used every method to upset them. He made the Children of Israel do dangerous work for little or no money. Years passed and the cruel kings continued to rule Egypt. One day the Pharaoh had a dream. In his vision, he saw an Israelite take him down from his throne.

exercises.title: The Pharaoh’s Fear
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 1.
exercises.question: Why was the Pharaoh rude and harsh to the Children of Israel?
options: They refused to do the dangerous work he gave them.
He was afraid that they would take control of his kingdom.
In a dream, he saw an Israelite take him down from his throne.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1 says: “The Pharaoh feared that this group … would take control of his kingdom. That’s why he was rude and harsh to the Children of Israel.” The dream came much later, after “Years passed”.

feedback.correct: Yes. His fear of losing his kingdom made him cruel to them.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the middle of Chapter 1. Find what the Pharaoh feared, just before the words “That’s why …”. Then check when the dream happened.

languageFocusExercises.title: Setting the Time or Moving It On?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each time phrase in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Does it give a time in history, or move the story on?

items: in the 13th century BC
over 3000 years ago
At that time, the Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
Years passed
One day the Pharaoh had a dream.

Places the story in history: At that time, the Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
Moves the story on: One day the Pharaoh had a dream.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “In the 13th century BC” and “over 3000 years ago” date the story; “ago” counts back from today. “At that time” points back to that same period and describes the situation in Egypt. “Years passed” jumps over a long period, and “One day” moves the story to one particular event: The dream.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated the expressions that date the story from the ones that move it forward.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the first sentences of Chapter 1, then at the last two. Which expressions give a date or a period, and which ones take us to a later time?

languageFocusExercises.title: Fear and Forced Work
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say the Pharaoh’s fear and his orders?

transformItems.source: The Pharaoh feared that this group, which was larger than the Egyptians, would take control of his kingdom.
transformItems.frame: The Pharaoh thought, “This group [blank] take control of my kingdom.”

transformItems.source: He made the Children of Israel do dangerous work for little or no money.
transformItems.frame: The Children of Israel [blank] do dangerous work for little or no money.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: In the Pharaoh’s own thoughts, the future is “will”: “This group will take control.” When the narrator reports that fear from a past point of view, “will” moves back to “would”: “feared that this group … would take control”. “Make + person + base verb” (made the Children of Israel do) shows that someone forced others to act. In the passive, “to” comes back: “The Children of Israel were made to do …”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You moved between the Pharaoh’s fear and his own words, and between “made … do” and “were made to do”.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the Pharaoh’s own words at that moment, and about the fact that the Children of Israel had no choice. Then check the middle of Chapter 1.

languageFocusExercises.title: Linking Reason and Result
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 1.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words give a result, and which show that something went on?

formChoices.sentence: They believed in Allah alone, just like their ancestor, Prophet Abraham (pbuh). [choice], they did not believe that the Pharaoh was a god.
The Pharaoh feared that this group … would take control of his kingdom. [choice] he was rude and harsh to the Children of Israel.
Years passed and the cruel kings continued [choice] Egypt.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “So” and “That’s why” both introduce a result. “That’s because” does the opposite: It introduces a reason. In the chapter, the belief and the fear are the reasons; not believing in the Pharaoh and the harsh treatment are the results. “Continue” is followed by “to + base verb” (or an -ing form): “continued to rule” shows that the situation went on for many years.

feedback.correct: Correct. You linked each reason to its result and showed that the situation continued.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: Is the next idea a reason or a result? Then check the second half of Chapter 1.

languageFocusExercises.title: A Story from History
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about another time in history.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you tell a short story from history?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong answer should create a coherent mini-paragraph rather than isolated sentences. Useful patterns include “At that time...”, “feared that... would...”, “that’s why...”, “made ... + verb”, and “continued to...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the sentences connected so each one develops the same situation.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the time: “At that time, …”
discussionPrompts.example: At that time, in the 1800s, a powerful company controlled the tea trade in our region.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what someone feared: “… feared that … would …”
discussionPrompts.example: The owners of the company feared that the small farmers would sell their tea to other buyers.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Add a result: “so …” or “That’s why …”
discussionPrompts.example: That’s why they kept the prices very low.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what someone made people do: “… made them …”
discussionPrompts.example: They made the farmers sell all their tea to the company.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say what went on: “… continued to …”
discussionPrompts.example: For many years, the company continued to control the market.

pages.title: The Pharaoh’s Dream
pages.content: Ibn Abbas said, “The Pharaoh saw a fire in his dream. The fire came from Jerusalem and burnt the houses of the Egyptians, but did not do any harm to the Children of Israel.” When he woke up, he called all his advisors and magicians and asked about the dream. They said, “A boy will be born of the Children of Israel and the Egyptian people will die at this boy’s hands.” Then, the Pharaoh told his soldiers, “Kill all the newborn boys of the Children of Israel.” His soldiers broke into houses and searched the rooms. When they found baby boys, they killed them. All mothers, fathers and sisters cried, but the soldiers who were heartless showed no pity. Moses (pbuh) was born in that year. His mother was so frightened that she was unable to sleep at night. She was scared that when Moses cried, the soldiers could hear his voice. She did not know what to do. She prayed to Allah for help. Allah heard her prayers and advised her, “Take a basket.”

exercises.title: From a Dream to a Prayer
exercises.instructions: Put the events of Chapter 2 in the right order.
exercises.question: What happened after the Pharaoh’s dream?

sequencingItems.text: The Pharaoh saw a fire in his dream.
The Pharaoh asked his advisors and magicians about the dream.
The magicians said that a boy of the Children of Israel would be born.
The Pharaoh ordered his soldiers to kill the newborn boys of the Children of Israel.
Moses’s mother, too frightened to sleep, prayed to Allah for help.

exercises.explanation: The Pharaoh saw the fire, then “called all his advisors and magicians and asked about the dream.” They said, “A boy will be born of the Children of Israel …”, so he gave the order to his soldiers. Moses was born in that year, and his mother “prayed to Allah for help.”

feedback.correct: Well done. Each step causes the next one: Fear leads to a cruel order, and the order leads to a mother’s prayer.
feedback.incorrect: Follow Chapter 2 from the beginning: The dream, the meeting about it, the order, and Moses’s mother at the end.

languageFocusExercises.title: A Prediction About the Future
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the advisors’ words. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: They said, “A boy will be born of the Children of Israel and the Egyptian people will die at this boy’s hands.” What are the advisors doing when they use “will”?
options: reporting something that has already happened in Egypt
giving the soldiers an order about the boys
predicting something that they believe is going to happen
describing something that happens every year in Egypt
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Will + base verb” is used here for a prediction: the advisors say what they believe is going to happen. “Will be born” is passive because a baby does not do the action of being born. The prediction leads to the Pharaoh’s order, which uses an imperative with no subject: “Kill …”.

feedback.correct: Correct. The advisors predict a future event, and the Pharaoh reacts to it.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: Has the boy been born yet when the advisors speak? Check what they said after the Pharaoh woke up.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Happened After the Dream?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 2 in order. “When” and “Then” can help.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened after the Pharaoh’s dream?

sequencingItems.text: When the Pharaoh woke up, he called all his advisors and magicians and asked about the dream.
Then, the Pharaoh told his soldiers, “Kill all the newborn boys of the Children of Israel.”
The Pharaoh’s soldiers broke into houses and searched the rooms.
When the soldiers found baby boys, they killed them.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “When he woke up” links his first action to the moment the dream ended. “Then” moves the story to the next step: The order. The imperative “Kill …” has no subject because it tells someone what to do. “When they found baby boys, they killed them” shows what happened each time the soldiers found a boy.

feedback.correct: Correct. The time words guided you from the dream to the soldiers’ actions.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the moment the Pharaoh woke up. Which sentence begins with “Then”? What did the soldiers do before they found the boys? Check the first half of Chapter 2.

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about the mother’s fear?

errorItems.sentence: His mother was such frightened that she was unable to sleep at night.
She was scared that when Moses cried, the soldiers can hear his voice.
She did not know what doing.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “So + adjective + that …” links a strong feeling to its result: So frightened that she was unable to sleep. “Such” goes before a noun (such a strong fear). After a past verb like “was scared that”, “can” moves back to “could”. “What to do” (question word + to + base verb) shows that she could not decide on her next action.

feedback.correct: Well done. You corrected the language of strong feeling, feared possibility and uncertainty.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each sentence with the end of Chapter 2, where Moses’s mother cannot sleep.

languageFocusExercises.title: Report a Warning and a Response
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about someone who gets a warning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happens after the warning?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Keep one situation across all five sentences. Useful patterns include “They said that/will...”, a direct imperative, “when...”, “so ... that...”, “was scared that ... could...”, and “did not know what to do”.

feedback.correct: Make the warning, emotional response, and final action form one connected mini-narrative.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the warning: “… warned that … would …”
discussionPrompts.example: The weather service warned that a big storm would reach our town the next day.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Give an order: “Stay … / Close …”
discussionPrompts.example: The mayor told everyone, “Stay at home and close your windows.”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Move the story on: “When …” or “Then …”
discussionPrompts.example: When the wind started, the streets became empty very quickly.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Show strong fear: “… was so scared that …”
discussionPrompts.example: My little brother was so scared that he could not sleep at all.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — End with a decision or a call for help.
discussionPrompts.example: My mother did not know what to do, so she called our neighbor for help.

pages.title: A Baby in the River
pages.content: “Put your baby in the basket. Take the basket to the River Nile. Waters will carry it to the shelter.” Moses’s mother put the baby Moses (pbuh) in a basket and took it to the river. There she put the basket in the water. The basket was carried away by the waters. Moses’s mother was very worried and told her daughter to follow the basket. She was so sad, but she knew that Allah was kinder to the baby Moses than she could be. Allah was their Lord and also the Lord of the Nile. Allah told the waves to be kind while carrying the baby. Soon, the waves brought the basket ashore near the Pharaoh’s palace. The palace servants saw the basket and took it to the Pharaoh and the queen, Asiye. When Queen Asiye saw the baby, she felt a strong love for him in her heart. The queen, who was different from her husband, was good, kind-hearted, and believed in Allah. While she was looking at the baby, she told her husband, “I will take him to the palace and look after him.”

exercises.title: A Mother’s Trust
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 3.
exercises.question: Moses’s mother was very sad. What gave her comfort when the waters carried her baby away?
options: Queen Asiye had promised her that she would look after the baby.
Her daughter promised to follow the basket and bring it back home.
She knew that Allah was kinder to the baby than she could be.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3 says: “She was so sad, but she knew that Allah was kinder to the baby Moses than she could be.” Her daughter only followed the basket, and Queen Asiye saw the baby later, at the palace.

feedback.correct: Right. Her trust in Allah was stronger than her sadness.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 3 again. Find the sentence that starts “She was so sad, but …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Why “Was Carried”?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentences from Chapter 3. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “There she put the basket in the water. The basket was carried away by the waters.” Why does the second sentence use “was carried”?
options: It shows that Moses’s mother carried the basket away.
It keeps the focus on the basket and on what happened to it.
It shows that the basket is still moving now.
It shows that the basket moved by itself.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: In a passive sentence (was/were + past participle), the thing that receives the action becomes the subject. The story is following the basket, so “The basket” comes first, and “by the waters” tells us what moved it. The mother’s part is over; now the basket is out of her hands.

feedback.correct: Correct. The passive keeps our attention on the basket.
feedback.incorrect: Who puts the basket in the water, and what carries it away? Read the first paragraph of Chapter 3 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Sadness, Trust and Time
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 3 with words from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words join the ideas in these lines?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: She was so sad, [blank] she knew that Allah was kinder to the baby Moses than she could be. Allah was their Lord and [blank] the Lord of the Nile. Allah told the waves to be kind [blank] carrying the baby. [blank], the waves brought the basket ashore near the Pharaoh’s palace.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “But” shows contrast: She was sad, and at the same time she trusted Allah. “Also” adds a second, similar idea (their Lord, and the Lord of the Nile too). “While + -ing” links two things happening at the same time. “Soon” moves the story a short time forward. “During” is followed by a noun (during the journey), not by an -ing verb like this, and “so” would introduce a result.

feedback.correct: Correct. You showed contrast, addition, time and sequence.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 3 again: Is her trust a contrast to her sadness or a result of it? Which word can come before “carrying”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Adding Information About the Queen
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to make the sentence from Chapter 3.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where does the extra information about the queen go?
sentenceChunks: who was different from her husband,
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A relative clause with “who” adds extra information about a person. It comes straight after the noun it describes and sits between commas: “The queen, who was different from her husband, was good …”. The main verb “was” comes after the second comma. This extra information prepares us for her decision: “I will take him to the palace and look after him.”

feedback.correct: Well done. The “who” clause sits between commas, right after “The queen”.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the person, add the information about her husband, and then give the main verb. Check the end of Chapter 3.

languageFocusExercises.title: Describe a Difficult Decision
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about someone who has to make a hard decision.
languageFocusExercises.question: What does the person feel, and what do they decide?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Keep one situation across all five sentences. Useful patterns include a direct imperative, a passive sentence, “but”, “while”, “when”, and “will” for a decision.

feedback.correct: Keep the paragraph connected so each sentence develops the same situation.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give an instruction: “Go to …”
discussionPrompts.example: My teacher said to me, “Register at the new school in the city.”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what happened next: “The next morning, I was taken …”
discussionPrompts.example: The next morning, I was taken to the city by my uncle.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Show worry and trust: “I was worried, but …”
discussionPrompts.example: I was very worried, but I knew that my teacher’s advice was good.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Add time: “When …” or “While …”
discussionPrompts.example: When I arrived at the school, the head teacher welcomed me with a smile.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — End with a decision: “I will …”
discussionPrompts.example: I said to myself, “I will study hard, and I will make new friends.”

pages.title: Back to His Mother
pages.content: The Pharaoh accepted her decision. She said to her servants, “Find a nurse for the baby.” Moses’ sister saw everything, and immediately ran to the Queen and said, “I know a good woman. She lives nearby. She will be a good nurse for the baby.” And she brought her mother to be Moses’s nurse in the palace. Allah sent Moses (pbuh) back to his mother, and baby Moses was in his mother’s arms again. Moses’ mother looked after her own baby. Allah is the Best Protector. Queen Asiye also took care of Moses and raised him in the palace with love. People always remember her because of her goodness and courage. Moses grew up safely in the palace of the Pharaoh. He always loved Allah and prayed to Him. He knew that the Pharaoh was not a god. Years passed and Moses became a strong young man. He was always willing to help the weak people. Young Moses felt close to the Children of Israel because he was originally not from a family of the palace and his mother was one of the Children of Israel.

exercises.title: Back in His Mother’s Arms
exercises.instructions: Match each person with what she did in Chapter 4.
exercises.question: How did baby Moses come back to his mother?

matchingPairs.right: told her servants to find a nurse for the baby
said she knew a good woman who lived nearby
looked after her own baby in the palace

correctAnswer.Queen Asiye: told her servants to find a nurse for the baby
correctAnswer.Moses’s sister: said she knew a good woman who lived nearby
correctAnswer.Moses’s mother: looked after her own baby in the palace

exercises.explanation: The queen said to her servants, “Find a nurse for the baby.” Moses’ sister ran to the Queen and said, “I know a good woman. She lives nearby.” Then “she brought her mother to be Moses’s nurse in the palace.” The chapter adds: “Allah is the Best Protector.”

feedback.correct: Well done. Each woman had a part, and Allah brought Moses back to his mother.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first half of Chapter 4 again. Follow who speaks first, who answers her, and who comes to the palace.

languageFocusExercises.title: Words About Care and Belonging
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word or phrase from Chapter 4 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words tell us about Moses’s life in the palace?

matchingPairs.right: at once, without waiting
not far away
brought him up as a child
had a strong connection with
at the start, by birth

correctAnswer.raised him: brought him up as a child

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Immediately” shows how quickly the sister acted. “Nearby” tells the Queen that the woman lives close. To “raise” a child is to look after them until they grow up. To “feel close to” people is to feel connected to them. “Originally” refers to where someone comes from at the start: Moses was not born into the palace family.

feedback.correct: Correct. These words show care, speed and belonging in Chapter 4.
feedback.incorrect: Find each word in Chapter 4 and use the sentence around it to work out its meaning.

languageFocusExercises.title: Purpose or Reason?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 4 with words from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words say why, and which say what for?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: And she brought her mother [blank] be Moses’s nurse in the palace. … People always remember her [blank] her goodness and courage. … Young Moses felt close to the Children of Israel [blank] he was originally not from a family of the palace and his mother was one of the Children of Israel.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “To + base verb” gives the purpose of an action: why she brought her mother. “Because of” is followed by a noun phrase (her goodness and courage). “Because” is followed by a full clause with a subject and a verb (he was originally not …). “For be” is not possible, and “so” would introduce a result, not a reason.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated purpose (to) from reason (because / because of).
feedback.incorrect: Look at what comes after each gap: A base verb, a noun phrase or a full clause? Then check Chapter 4.

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about Moses growing up?

errorItems.sentence: She will is a good nurse for the baby.
Years passed and Moses become a strong young man.
He was always willing helping the weak people.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “will”, use the base verb: “will be”. The sister is confident about the future. “Became” is the past of “become” and shows a change into a new state (a strong young man). “Willing” is followed by “to + base verb”: willing to help. With “always”, it describes a lasting quality of his character.

feedback.correct: Well done. You corrected the prediction, the change and the personal quality.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each sentence with Chapter 4: the sister’s words to the Queen, and the last paragraph about Moses as a young man.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain How a Person Grows into a Role
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about someone who gets help and grows.
languageFocusExercises.question: How does the person change over time?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Keep one situation across all five sentences. Useful patterns include an imperative, “to + verb” for purpose, “because/because of” for reason, “became” for change, and “always” for a continuing tendency.

feedback.correct: Keep the account connected so each sentence develops the same person and situation.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give a piece of advice: “Watch … and learn …”
discussionPrompts.example: The coach told the new player, “Watch the older players and learn from them.”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what for: “… to + verb”
discussionPrompts.example: The boy came to every training session to improve his skills.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give a reason: “because …”
discussionPrompts.example: He trained very hard because he loved the game.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Show a change: “After three years, he became …”
discussionPrompts.example: After three years, he became the captain of the team.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say what the person always does now.
discussionPrompts.example: He always helps the younger players when they make mistakes.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: Who also took care of Moses and raised him with love?
beforeYouRead.quote: Queen Asiye also took care of Moses and raised him in the palace with love.

steps: Read your chapter again. Note two important events and one sentence from the book that gives a reason or a result.
Teach your events to the group in your own words, then read your sentence from the book aloud.
Listen to the others and put all the events in order on one shared timeline.

Together, finish this sentence with two reasons from the book: The Children of Israel were in danger because … For example, “The Pharaoh feared that this group, which was larger than the Egyptians, would take control of his kingdom.”
groupTask.share: Each group shows its timeline and reads one quote that shows the danger and one quote that shows how the baby was kept safe, such as “Allah is the Best Protector.”
groupTask.solo: Write one event from each of Chapters 1–4 in the right order, then copy one sentence from the book that gives a reason for one of the events.

pages.title: A Mistake in the Bazaar
pages.content: One day, while Moses (pbuh) was walking in the bazaar, he saw two men fighting. One of them was an Egyptian, while the other was from the Children of Israel. Suddenly, a poor and weak man from the Children of Israel called out, “Help me!” Moses ran to help him. He hit the Egyptian and accidentally caused someone’s death. Moses was very upset. He prayed to Allah, “Forgive me! I didn’t do it on purpose. I have wronged myself. This is of Satan’s doing.” (Surah al-Qasas: 15–16) Allah pardoned him because He is Forgiving and Merciful. The next day, Moses was again in the bazaar where he saw two men fighting. One of them was the same man from the Children of Israel who Moses helped the day before. The man once more called out to Moses, “Help me!” Moses understood that the Israelite was a quarrelsome man, not a peaceable man. Moses approached those who were fighting. The man from the Children of Israel made fun of Moses, “You accidentally caused someone’s death yesterday. Are you going to kill me too?”

hotspots.title: The Mistake
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) accidentally caused the Egyptian’s death while he was trying to help.

hotspots.title: Forgiveness
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) prayed to Allah after his mistake, and Allah pardoned him.

exercises.title: Sorry for a Mistake
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 5.
exercises.question: Why did Moses pray, “Forgive me!”?
options: He had caused a man’s death, although he did not mean to.
The man from the Children of Israel made fun of him.
The Pharaoh’s soldiers were looking for him.
exercises.explanation: Moses hit the Egyptian and caused his death by accident. He was very upset and prayed, “I didn’t do it on purpose. I have wronged myself.” The man made fun of him only the next day, and the soldiers come in Chapter 6.

feedback.correct: Yes. Moses took responsibility for his mistake and asked Allah to forgive him.
feedback.incorrect: Read the beginning of Chapter 5 again. Look at what happened just before Moses prayed.

languageFocusExercises.title: Which Action Was in Progress?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 5. Is the statement true or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: “One day, while Moses (pbuh) was walking in the bazaar, he saw two men fighting.” This means that Moses finished his walk first, and after that he saw the two men.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “While + past continuous” (was walking) describes a longer action that was already in progress. The past simple (saw) is a shorter event that happened in the middle of it. So Moses was still walking when he saw the fight. After that, “Suddenly” brings in a new, unexpected action: The man calls out for help.

feedback.correct: Correct. The walking was still in progress when he saw the fight.
feedback.incorrect: Look at “while … was walking”. Was the walk finished, or still happening, when he saw the men? Check the first sentence of Chapter 5.

languageFocusExercises.title: The Next Day
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 5.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened the next day, and what did Moses understand?

formChoices.sentence: The next day, Moses was again in the bazaar where he [choice] two men fighting.
One of them was the same man from the Children of Israel [choice] Moses helped the day before.
Moses understood [choice] the Israelite was a quarrelsome man, not a peaceable man.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The past simple “saw” reports a single finished event; “see” is not normally used in the continuous with this meaning. “Who” begins a relative clause about a person: The same man who Moses helped the day before. “Understood that …” introduces a conclusion that Moses reached from what he saw: The man was fighting again.

feedback.correct: Correct. You reported the event, identified the man and introduced Moses’s conclusion.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second half of Chapter 5 again. Is the man a person or a thing? What comes after “understood” when a full clause follows?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Are the Speakers Doing?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each spoken line from Chapter 5 with what the speaker is doing.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who asks, who admits and who accuses?

matchingPairs.right: calls urgently for support
asks to be pardoned

matchingPairs.left: I didn’t do it on purpose.
matchingPairs.right: says that the harm was not intended
admits having done something wrong

matchingPairs.left: Are you going to kill me too?
matchingPairs.right: accuses someone by asking a question

says that the harm was not intended
correctAnswer.Are you going to kill me too?: accuses someone by asking a question

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Short imperatives (Help me! Forgive me!) make urgent requests. “On purpose” means deliberately, so “I didn’t do it on purpose” means it was an accident. “I have wronged myself” uses the present perfect: A past action whose result matters now, so Moses admits his mistake. “Are you going to …?” asks about a next action, but here it is an accusation, not a real question.

feedback.correct: Correct. You recognized requests, an admission and an accusation.
feedback.incorrect: Read Moses’s prayer and the man’s last words in Chapter 5 again. Who is asking for help, who is sorry, and who is blaming someone?

languageFocusExercises.title: Tell a Short Incident Clearly
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about a fight or argument in the street.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you tell what happened, step by step?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Keep one situation throughout. Useful patterns include “while + past continuous”, “suddenly”, a relative clause with “who”, “understood/realized that”, and a question with “going to”.

feedback.correct: Keep the five sentences connected and make each one develop the same event.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Set the scene: “While I was …ing, …”
discussionPrompts.example: While I was waiting at the bus stop, two drivers were arguing in the street.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Add a surprise: “Suddenly, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Suddenly, one of them got out of his car and started to shout.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Describe a person: “A man who … came …”
discussionPrompts.example: A man who worked in the shop nearby came out to calm them down.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what someone understood: “He realized that …”
discussionPrompts.example: He realized that the whole problem was only a small scratch on a car.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — End with a question: “Are you going to …?”
discussionPrompts.example: He asked them, “Are you going to stand here and shout all day?”

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: Who were the two men fighting in the bazaar?
options: an Egyptian and a man from the Children of Israel
beforeYouRead.quote: One of them was an Egyptian, while the other was from the Children of Israel.

iCan: I can tell what happened in the bazaar on two days.
I can say what was happening when something sudden happened.
I can tell a short incident clearly in five sentences.

pages.title: Escape from Egypt
pages.content: His sadness increased even more. At this moment a man came from the far end of the city and said to Moses (pbuh), “The Pharaoh’s soldiers are looking for you. You killed an Egyptian yesterday. Now they are going to catch you. Run away from the city.” Moses knew that the punishment for killing an Egyptian was death. Moses escaped from the soldiers. He left Egypt and traveled for a long time. He was not alone as Allah guided him. After many days, he reached the land of Midian, which was the closest place between Egypt and Syria. The Pharaoh was not the ruler in this land. Moses was tired and thirsty. He was looking for water. Soon, he found a well where many men gathered. These were shepherds who were watering their sheep and cattle. Far from the spring two girls were sitting. They also had sheep with them. But they did not go near it. Moses asked the girls, “Why are you sitting far away from the spring? Why aren’t you taking your sheep to drink water?”

hotspots.title: A Warning
hotspots.description: A man from the city warned Moses (pbuh) that the Pharaoh’s soldiers were looking for him, so he left Egypt.

hotspots.title: The Well in Midian
hotspots.description: In Midian, Moses (pbuh) found shepherds at a well and two girls waiting far from the water.

exercises.title: Safe in Midian
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 6.
exercises.question: When Moses reached Midian, he was in a land that the Pharaoh did not rule.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says: “The Pharaoh was not the ruler in this land.” So in Midian, Moses was out of the reach of the Pharaoh’s soldiers.

feedback.correct: Correct. The Pharaoh did not rule Midian, so it was a safer place for Moses.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 6 again. Find the sentence about who ruled the land of Midian.

languageFocusExercises.title: Now and Next
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the man’s warning from Chapter 6. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: A man from the city says to Moses, “The Pharaoh’s soldiers are looking for you. … Now they are going to catch you.” Why does the man use “are going to”?
options: The soldiers have already caught Moses and taken him to the Pharaoh.
The soldiers catch people like Moses every day, so it is a habit for them.
The man is promising to help the soldiers find Moses in the city.
He expects it to happen soon because the soldiers are already searching.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Be going to” makes a prediction based on what is happening now. The evidence is in the present continuous: “are looking for you” – the search is already in progress. That is why the man then gives an urgent imperative: “Run away from the city.”

feedback.correct: Correct. The man predicts the next step from what is already happening.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the sentence before “are going to”: What are the soldiers doing right now? Check the first paragraph of Chapter 6.

languageFocusExercises.title: From Egypt to Midian
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts of Chapter 6 in the right order.
languageFocusExercises.question: How did Moses get from Egypt to Midian?

sequencingItems.text: Moses knew that the punishment for killing an Egyptian was death.
Moses escaped from the soldiers.
Moses left Egypt and traveled for a long time.
After many days, Moses reached the land of Midian …
Moses was tired and thirsty. He was looking for water.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Knew that …” gives the reason for his decision. Then a chain of past simple verbs (escaped, left, traveled) moves the journey forward. “After many days” marks a new point after a long time. In the new place, the past continuous “was looking for” describes what he was doing when the next scene begins.

feedback.correct: Correct. You followed the reason, the journey and the arrival.
feedback.incorrect: Start with what Moses knew. Which phrase shows that a long time has passed? Check the middle of Chapter 6.

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about the well?

errorItems.sentence: Soon, he found a well which many men gathered.
These were shepherds which were watering their sheep and cattle.
Moses asked the girls, “Why you are sitting far away from the spring?”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Where” begins a relative clause about a place: A well where many men gathered. “Who” is used for people: Shepherds who were watering their sheep. In a question with a question word, the auxiliary comes before the subject: “Why are you sitting …?” Moses uses the present continuous because he is asking about what he can see at that moment.

feedback.correct: Well done. You corrected the place clause, the person clause and the question.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each sentence with the last paragraph of Chapter 6. Is the clause about a place or about people? Where does “are” go in a question?

languageFocusExercises.title: Leaving in a Hurry
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about someone who must leave a place quickly.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the danger, and where does the person go?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Keep one situation throughout. Useful patterns include present continuous for a current threat, “be going to” for an expected consequence, an imperative, “after + time”, and a “Why are you ...?” question about a visible situation.

feedback.correct: Keep the five sentences connected and make the final scene follow naturally from the warning.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what is happening now: “The water is rising!”
discussionPrompts.example: Our neighbor shouted, “The water in the river is rising fast!”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what will happen next: “It is going to …”
discussionPrompts.example: “It is going to reach our houses tonight.”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give an order: “Leave now and …!”
discussionPrompts.example: “Leave your houses now and go up the hill!”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say where they arrived: “After …, we arrived at …”
discussionPrompts.example: After two hours of walking, we arrived at a school on the hill that we had never seen before.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Ask a question: “Why are you …?”
discussionPrompts.example: I asked a man at the door, “Why are you giving out blankets?”

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: Where was the land of Midian?
beforeYouRead.quote: which was the closest place between Egypt and Syria

iCan: I can explain why Moses (pbuh) left Egypt and where he went.
I can say what is happening now and what is going to happen next.
I can write about leaving a place and arriving somewhere new.

pages.title: The Two Sisters
pages.content: The girls said, “Our father is very old. He cannot come with us. There are no young men in our house to help us with the animals. So, we have to take the sheep to the water ourselves. We have to wait our turn. We have to be patient until the other shepherds go away.” Moses (pbuh) understood that the two sisters needed help. He took their sheep to the spring and gave them water. The girls were very happy. They took their sheep and went home. When the sisters came home early, their father asked, “What happened? You came home very early!” The sisters said, “A young man helped us to water our sheep. We did not have to wait until the other shepherds went away.” The father of these girls was Shu’ayb (pbuh). Shu’ayb (pbuh) was a messenger of Allah to the eastern part of the Gulf of Aqaba, Midian. Prophet Shu’ayb (pbuh) was very old. That’s why he had to send the girls alone.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-midian
__historical_entity__:moses-gulf-of-aqaba
The time when you can do something after other people.
People who look after sheep.
A person chosen to deliver Allah’s message.
Having lived for a great many years.

hotspots.title: Waiting Their Turn
hotspots.description: The sisters waited because their father was very old and they had no one else to help.

hotspots.title: Helping Others
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) watered the sisters’ sheep, so they returned home early.

exercises.title: Home Early
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 7.
exercises.question: Why did the two sisters get home early that day?
options: Their old father called them back home.
A young man watered their sheep, so they did not wait for their turn.
The other shepherds let them take their sheep to the water first.
exercises.explanation: The sisters told their father: “A young man helped us to water our sheep. We did not have to wait until the other shepherds went away.”

feedback.correct: Right. Moses saw that they needed help, and his kindness saved them a long wait.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 7 again. Find what the sisters told their father when he asked, “What happened?”

languageFocusExercises.title: Necessary or Not?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sisters’ words from Chapter 7. Then choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: The sisters tell their father, “We did not have to wait …” What does “did not have to wait” mean?
options: They were not allowed to wait.
Waiting was not necessary that day.
They waited, but only for a short time.
They did not want to wait, so they left.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Have to” shows that something is necessary. “Did not have to” means it was not necessary – there was no need – because Moses had already watered their sheep. It does not mean “not allowed”; for that meaning we use “were not allowed to” or “must not”.

feedback.correct: Correct. The usual waiting was not necessary that day.
feedback.incorrect: Why did the sisters come home early? Read what they tell their father in Chapter 7.

languageFocusExercises.title: Why the Sisters Wait
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the sisters’ words from Chapter 7. Use the word bank. Three words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Why did the sisters wait at the well?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Our father is very old. He [blank] come with us. There are no young men in our house to help us with the animals. [blank], we have to take the sheep to the water ourselves. We have to wait our turn. We have to be patient [blank] the other shepherds go away.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Cannot” shows that the father is not able to come. “So” introduces the result: Nobody can help, so the girls have to do the work themselves. “Have to” shows necessity. “Until” gives the end point of the waiting. “Must not” would mean he is not allowed to come, and “when” would not show how long they wait.

feedback.correct: Correct. You linked the problem, its result and the end of the waiting.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 7 again. Is the father not able to come, or not allowed to come? How long do the girls wait?

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It Another Way
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say these lines from Chapter 7?

transformItems.source: Prophet Shu’ayb (pbuh) was very old. That’s why he had to send the girls alone.
transformItems.frame: Prophet Shu’ayb (pbuh) had to send the girls alone [blank] he was very old.

transformItems.source: There are no young men in our house to help us with the animals.
transformItems.frame: We do not have [blank] young men in our house to help us with the animals.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “That’s why” introduces a result; “because” introduces a reason, so the order of the ideas changes. “There are no + noun” and “do not have any + noun” both say that something is missing. Here the missing help is the reason why the sisters have to do the work themselves.

feedback.correct: Well done. You turned the result into a reason and described the missing help in another way.
feedback.incorrect: Which idea is the reason: Shu’ayb’s age or sending the girls alone? Which word goes with “do not have” before a plural noun?

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain a Routine That Changes
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about people who get help one day.
languageFocusExercises.question: What changes when someone helps?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Keep one situation throughout. Useful patterns include “cannot”, “have to”, “until”, a simple-past action that changes the situation, and “did not have to” for an obligation that disappears.

feedback.correct: Keep the five sentences connected and make the changed result follow naturally from the help.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what is missing: “Our village has no …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our village has no bus to the market in town.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what people have to do: “So, they have to …”
discussionPrompts.example: So, the farmers have to carry their vegetables there on foot.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say how long they wait: “They wait until …”
discussionPrompts.example: They usually wait by the road until a truck stops for them.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say who helped: “One day, … helped …”
discussionPrompts.example: One day, a young teacher drove all the farmers to the market in his van.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say what changed: “They did not have to …”
discussionPrompts.example: They did not have to wait by the road for hours because the teacher helped them.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: Why did the two girls water their sheep themselves?
options: They liked the work very much.
Their father was very old and could not come with them.
beforeYouRead.quote: Our father is very old. He cannot come with us.

iCan: I can explain why the two sisters waited at the well.
I can say what people have to do and did not have to do.
I can explain how help changed someone’s daily routine.

pages.title: A Simple Life in Midian
pages.content: Shu’ayb (pbuh) said, “Go and call the young man, I would like to thank him for the work he did.” Moses (pbuh) came to the house, where he ate food with the girls’ father. Shu’ayb (pbuh) offered Moses a job. He accepted the offer because he was a stranger in Midian and he urgently needed a job and a house. Moses helped the family with their work while he was staying with them. Later, he married one of the sisters. They lived a simple life with patience. After living in Midian for about ten years, with the guidance of Allah, Moses decided to go back to Egypt. He took his family and started to travel towards Egypt. They traveled a long time. It was winter. They met nobody on the way. It was getting dark and cold. They were crossing a valley between mountains. Suddenly, Moses saw a fire on the hillside. He said to his family, “Wait here. Let me go and take some burning sticks from the fire to get warm.”

__historical_entity__:moses-midian
__historical_entity__:moses-valley-of-tuwa
Gave someone a chance to accept something.
A person who is new to a place and does not know people there.
Low land between hills or mountains.
The sloping side of a small mountain.

hotspots.title: A New Family
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) accepted work, married one of the sisters, and lived in Midian for about ten years.

hotspots.title: The Fire
hotspots.description: On the journey back to Egypt, Moses (pbuh) saw a fire on the hillside.

exercises.title: From Midian Towards Egypt
exercises.instructions: Put the events of Chapter 8 in the right order.
exercises.question: How did Moses’s life in Midian lead to a new journey?

sequencingItems.text: Shu’ayb (pbuh) asked for the young man to come so that he could thank him.
Moses accepted a job because he needed work and a house.
Moses married one of the sisters.
After about ten years, Moses started to travel to Egypt with his family.
On a dark, cold evening, Moses saw a fire on the hillside.

exercises.explanation: Shu’ayb (pbuh) called Moses to thank him and offered him a job. “Later, he married one of the sisters.” “After living in Midian for about ten years”, Moses took his family towards Egypt, and on the winter journey he saw a fire.

feedback.correct: Well done. Ten patient years in Midian came before the journey back to Egypt.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the time words in Chapter 8: “Later”, “After living in Midian for about ten years” and “Suddenly”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Background or Main Event?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Is it the background or a main event? Put each part in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: How does the winter scene begin?

items: It was winter.
It was getting dark and cold.
They were crossing a valley between mountains.
He took his family and started to travel towards Egypt.
Suddenly, Moses saw a fire on the hillside.
He said to his family, “Wait here. …”

Background (the situation): It was getting dark and cold.
They were crossing a valley between mountains.
Main event (what happened): He took his family and started to travel towards Egypt.
Suddenly, Moses saw a fire on the hillside.
He said to his family, “Wait here. …”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Background sentences describe the situation: “was” + a noun or adjective (It was winter), or the past continuous for something in progress or changing (was getting dark, were crossing). Main events use the past simple (took, started, saw, said). “Suddenly” marks an event that breaks into the background.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated the scene from the actions that move the story on.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verbs: “was/were + -ing” or “was + adjective” describes the scene; the past simple tells what happened. Check the last paragraph of Chapter 8.

languageFocusExercises.title: Words from Life in Midian
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word or phrase from Chapter 8 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words tell us about Moses’s life in Midian?

matchingPairs.right: a person from another place
very quickly because it could not wait
calmly, without complaining
the sloping side of a mountain
pieces of wood that are on fire

correctAnswer.urgently: very quickly because it could not wait
correctAnswer.hillside: the sloping side of a mountain
correctAnswer.burning sticks: pieces of wood that are on fire

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “A stranger” and “urgently” explain why Moses accepted the job: He was new in Midian and needed work and a home quickly. “With patience” describes how the family lived. “Hillside” and “burning sticks” build the winter scene and Moses’s plan to get warm.

feedback.correct: Correct. These words explain Moses’s decision and build the scene.
feedback.incorrect: Find each word in Chapter 8 and use the sentence around it to work out its meaning.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It Another Way
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say these lines from Chapter 8?

transformItems.source: After living in Midian for about ten years, with the guidance of Allah, Moses decided to go back to Egypt.
transformItems.frame: After Moses [blank] in Midian for about ten years, he decided to go back to Egypt.

transformItems.source: He accepted the offer because he was a stranger in Midian and he urgently needed a job and a house.
transformItems.frame: He was a stranger in Midian and he urgently needed a job and a house, [blank] he accepted the offer.

transformItems.source: Let me go and take some burning sticks from the fire to get warm.
transformItems.frame: Let me go and take some burning sticks from the fire so that we [blank] warm.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “After + -ing” (After living …) is a short way to say “After he had lived …”. “Because” introduces a reason; “so” introduces a result, so the order of the ideas changes. “To + base verb” shows purpose (to get warm); “so that + subject + can/will” says the same thing with a full clause.

feedback.correct: Well done. You expressed time, result and purpose with new structures.
feedback.incorrect: Check the verb form after “After Moses …”, think about whether the missing word introduces a reason or a result, and remember that “so that” needs a subject and a verb such as “can”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain a Change of Plan
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about someone who changes plans suddenly.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did the person plan, and what changed?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Keep one situation throughout. Useful language includes “After living/working...”, “decided to...”, a past-progressive background sentence, “Suddenly...”, and “to + verb” for purpose.

feedback.correct: Keep the five sentences connected so the sudden event naturally changes what the person does next.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say how long: “After working there for … years, …”
discussionPrompts.example: After working in the city for twelve years, my uncle was tired of the noise.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Give a decision: “He decided to …”
discussionPrompts.example: He decided to move back to his village.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Set the scene: “He was driving …, and it was getting …”
discussionPrompts.example: He was driving home on a rainy evening, and it was getting dark.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Add a surprise: “Suddenly, he saw …”
discussionPrompts.example: Suddenly, he saw a car that had stopped at the side of the road.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say what he did and why: “He stopped to …”
discussionPrompts.example: He stopped his own car to help the family inside.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: Who did they meet on the way?
beforeYouRead.quote: They met nobody on the way.

iCan: I can tell about the life of Moses (pbuh) in Midian and his journey back.
I can show the background and the main event of a story.
I can explain a change of plan in five sentences.

pages.title: The Voice on the Mountain
pages.content: Moses (pbuh) climbed the mountain. It was already dark and everywhere was very quiet. In the silence he heard a thundering voice: “Moses, I am your Lord. I chose you. Listen to me. I am Allah. There is no god but Allah. Remember Me and pray to Me.” Then Allah told Moses, “Put down your walking stick!” Moses put down his staff on the ground. It turned into a big snake! Once more Allah spoke to Moses, “Put your hand into your chest. Now take it out. See, your hand is now shining like silver. But it is not harmed.” Allah said, “These are signs of My power. Show these signs to the Pharaoh. And tell him of the power of Allah.” Allah told Moses to go to Egypt and show the Pharaoh the signs and warn him to get guidance from Allah. After this message from Allah, Moses became a Messenger of Allah, a prophet. (See Surah Taha: 9–24.) Upon this, Moses (pbuh) headed to Egypt.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-egypt-ancient
__historical_entity__:moses-mount-sinai
__historical_entity__:moses-pharaoh
A state in which there is no sound at all.
A long stick used for walking or support.
Miracles or proofs of Allah’s power.
Help and direction that show a person the right way to live.

hotspots.title: The Call
hotspots.description: Allah called Moses (pbuh) on the mountain and gave him a mission.

hotspots.title: Staff and Shining Hand
hotspots.description: The staff and the shining hand were signs of Allah’s power.

exercises.title: Signs of Power
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 9.
exercises.question: Why did Allah show Moses the staff and the shining hand?
options: to help Moses bring fire back to his family
to make the Children of Israel follow Moses out of Egypt
to show the Pharaoh the power of Allah
exercises.explanation: Allah said: “These are signs of My power. Show these signs to the Pharaoh. And tell him of the power of Allah.”

feedback.correct: Yes. The signs were for the Pharaoh, to warn him and call him to Allah’s guidance.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 9 again. Find what Allah says right after the shining hand.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Upon This” Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the last sentence of Chapter 9. Then choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: After the message on the mountain, the chapter ends: “Upon this, Moses (pbuh) headed to Egypt.” What does “Upon this” mean here?
options: on top of this mountain, at that place
right after this, and because of it
before this happened, some time earlier
even though this had happened to him
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Upon this” is a formal connector. It links an event with the action that follows it immediately, as a response. The message from Allah comes first, and heading to Egypt is Moses’s response. To “head to” a place means to go towards it.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Upon this” shows an action that follows as a response.
feedback.incorrect: What had just happened before Moses went to Egypt? Read the last three sentences of Chapter 9.

languageFocusExercises.title: Change, Mission and New Role
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 9.
languageFocusExercises.question: What changed on the mountain, and what was Moses told to do?

formChoices.sentence: Moses put down his staff on the ground. It [choice] a big snake!
Allah told Moses [choice] to Egypt and show the Pharaoh the signs …
After this message from Allah, Moses [choice] a Messenger of Allah, a prophet.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Turn into” shows a complete change from one thing into another. “Tell + person + to + base verb” reports an instruction without quoting it: Allah told Moses to go … and show … and warn …. “Became” marks a new role; “After this message” shows what came first.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the forms for change, reported instruction and new role.
feedback.incorrect: Check the second half of Chapter 9: what happens to the staff, what Moses is told to do, and what he becomes.

languageFocusExercises.title: On the Mountain
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts of Chapter 9 in order. “Then” and “Once more” can help.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did Allah say, and what did Moses do?

sequencingItems.text: Moses climbed the mountain.
In the silence he heard a thundering voice …
Then Allah told Moses, “Put down your walking stick!”
Moses put down his staff on the ground.
Once more Allah spoke to Moses …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Then” and “Once more” show the order of Allah’s words. Each command is an imperative with no subject (“Put down …!”), and Moses’s action follows in the past simple (“put down”). This command → action → result pattern runs through the whole chapter.

feedback.correct: Correct. You followed the scene from the voice to the command and Moses’s action.
feedback.incorrect: The voice comes before the command, and the command comes before Moses’s action. Which word shows that Allah spoke a second time?

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain a New Responsibility
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about someone who gets a new job or duty.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the person told to do, and what changes?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Keep one situation throughout. Useful language includes an imperative, “told + person + to...”, “After this...”, “became...”, and a final sentence showing the next action.

feedback.correct: Keep the five sentences connected so the responsibility develops clearly from instruction to action.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give an instruction: “Look after …”
discussionPrompts.example: “Look after the school garden this year,” the head teacher said to my friend.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Report it: “She told my friend to …”
discussionPrompts.example: She told my friend to water the plants every morning.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what happened: “She did it, and soon …”
discussionPrompts.example: My friend watered them every day, and soon the garden was full of flowers.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Show the new duty: “After this, she became …”
discussionPrompts.example: After this, she became the leader of the garden club.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say what she does now.
discussionPrompts.example: Now she teaches the younger students how to plant seeds.

I can report what someone told another person to do.
I can explain how a person takes on a new responsibility.

groupTask.title: From Egypt to the Mountain

roles.name: Reader A (Egypt)
roles.job: You know Chapters 5–6: why Moses (pbuh) had to leave Egypt and where he arrived.

roles.name: Reader B (Midian)

steps: Each reader reads only his or her chapters and then closes the book.
The Map Keeper asks each reader: Where did he go? Why did he go there? How long did he stay?
Each reader answers with one sentence from the book, for example: “He left Egypt and traveled for a long time.” The Map Keeper adds the place and the reason to the route.
Together, check your route against the map page “Moses’s Journey” in the app and correct anything you placed wrongly.
