groupTask.solo: Cover Chapters 5–9, draw the route Egypt → Midian → the mountain from memory with one reason for each move, then check it on the map page “Moses’s Journey”.

pages.title: The King’s Magicians
pages.content: Allah chose Moses (pbuh) to be His prophet. Moses (pbuh) took his brother Harun (pbuh) with him as his companion and went to the palace. The king was sitting on his throne, and his advisors and soldiers were standing around him. Moses (pbuh) told him about Allah. He explained to him that he was the Messenger from the Lord of the universe. The king listened to Moses (pbuh) and he thought Moses had lost his mind. After making every effort to convince him, Moses (pbuh) realized that logical discussions would not work. The Pharaoh kept refusing to believe in Allah. Moses (pbuh) had no choice but to display the miracles. Moses (pbuh) got his staff and threw it on the ground. The staff turned into a big snake! Then he put his arm in his armpit. When he took his arm out, it was shining white! These were miracles of Allah. Allah gave them to Moses (pbuh) in order to help him against the Pharaoh. The king and his advisors laughed at him.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-pharaohs-palace
__historical_entity__:moses-pharaoh
Hard work that you do to try to achieve something.
A special seat for a king or ruler.
Everything that exists, including all space, stars and planets.
To show something so that people can see it.

hotspots.title: Harun
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) took his brother Harun (pbuh) with him when he went to the Pharaoh.

hotspots.title: Signs in the Palace
hotspots.description: When words did not convince the Pharaoh, Moses (pbuh) showed him the staff and the shining hand.

exercises.title: Words Before Miracles
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 10.
exercises.question: Moses showed the Pharaoh the miracles as soon as he arrived at the palace.
exercises.explanation: First, Moses “told him about Allah”. After “making every effort to convince him”, he “realized that logical discussions would not work.” Only then did he have “no choice but to display the miracles.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Moses tried to convince the Pharaoh with words first; the miracles came later.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 10 again. What did Moses do first, before he threw down his staff?

languageFocusExercises.title: Only One Option Left
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 10. Then choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Moses (pbuh) had no choice but to display the miracles.” What does “had no choice but to” mean?
options: He did not want to show the miracles, so he stopped.
He could choose from many different ways.
Showing the miracles was the only thing he could still do.
Someone else showed the miracles for him.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Have no choice but to + base verb” means that the other options have failed, so only one action is left. The sentences before it explain why: Talking and logical discussion did not work, and the Pharaoh went on refusing.

feedback.correct: Correct. Only one option was left for Moses.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentences just before this one in Chapter 10. Did Moses’s first way of convincing the Pharaoh work?

languageFocusExercises.title: Action and Visible Result
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts of Chapter 10 in order. “Then” and “When” can help.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did Moses do, and what happened each time?

sequencingItems.text: Moses (pbuh) got his staff and threw it on the ground.
The staff turned into a big snake!
Then Moses put his arm in his armpit.
When Moses took his arm out, it was shining white!
The king and his advisors laughed at him.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Each action is followed by its result. “Then” moves to the second action, and “When he took his arm out” links that action to the new state (it was shining white). The last sentence is a contrast: The signs were real miracles, but the king and his advisors only laughed.

feedback.correct: Correct. You followed each action to its result and to the king’s reaction.
feedback.incorrect: An action comes before its result. Which sentence begins with “Then”, and which one begins with “When”? Check the end of Chapter 10.

languageFocusExercises.title: Effort, Repetition and Purpose
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say these lines from Chapter 10?

transformItems.source: After making every effort to convince him, Moses (pbuh) realized that logical discussions would not work.
transformItems.frame: After he [blank] every effort to convince him, Moses (pbuh) realized that logical discussions would not work.

transformItems.source: The Pharaoh kept refusing to believe in Allah.
transformItems.frame: The Pharaoh refused to believe in Allah again and [blank].

transformItems.source: Allah gave them to Moses (pbuh) in order to help him against the Pharaoh.
transformItems.frame: Allah gave them to Moses (pbuh) so that they [blank] help him against the Pharaoh.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “After + -ing” can be expanded into a full clause: “After he had made every effort …”. “Keep + -ing” shows that an action happens again and again. “In order to + base verb” and “so that + subject + could/would” both express purpose.

feedback.correct: Well done. You expressed the same ideas with new structures.
feedback.incorrect: Use the past form of “make” after “After he …”, think about what “kept refusing” says about how often he refused, and use a modal such as “could” after “so that they”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain a Change of Approach
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about someone who tries a new way to solve a problem.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did the person try first, and what did they do next?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Keep one situation throughout. Useful language includes “After making every effort...”, “realized that...”, “kept...”, “had no choice but to...”, “When...”, “turned into/became...”, and “in order to...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the five sentences connected so the change of approach is easy to follow.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what they tried first: “We tried to …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our class tried to fix the old projector for a whole hour, but it still did not work.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what they understood: “… realized that …”
discussionPrompts.example: After many tries, our teacher realized that the projector was too old to repair.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give the next step: “She had no choice but to …”
discussionPrompts.example: She had no choice but to write the lesson on the board.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Give the result: “When she …, everyone …”
discussionPrompts.example: When she drew the pictures on the board, everyone understood the lesson.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say why: “She did it in order to …”
discussionPrompts.example: She drew them in order to help us follow the lesson without the projector.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: Why did Allah give Moses (pbuh) the miracles?
options: to help him against the Pharaoh
beforeYouRead.quote: Allah gave them to Moses (pbuh) in order to help him against the Pharaoh.

iCan: I can explain why Moses (pbuh) showed the miracles to the king.
I can say what someone tried, realized and then did.
I can explain a change of approach in five sentences.

pages.title: The Miracle of the Staff
pages.content: They made fun of Moses (pbuh) and Allah’s signs. The king said to Moses (pbuh), “This is only magic. All of my magicians can do this.” He invited his magicians to the palace. The magicians came with sticks in their hands. Some were holding ropes. They put down the sticks and ropes. Once the sticks and ropes fell to the ground, they looked just like snakes! When Moses (pbuh) saw them, he got frightened. But Allah spoke to Moses (pbuh), “Throw down your staff!” Moses (pbuh) threw down his staff and it turned into a huge snake. In a second, his staff ate up all the snakes of the magicians. The magicians who witnessed this miracle bowed down to Allah. They shouted, “We believe in the Lord of Moses and Harun!” The king still refused to believe in Allah because he was arrogant. The Pharaoh did not want to let those who worshipped Allah live. He continued to trouble Moses (pbuh) and his people day and night. He told his advisors and soldiers, “Be rude to them!”

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-pharaohs-palace
__historical_entity__:moses-pharaoh
__historical_entity__:moses-pharaohs-magicians
Laughed at someone in an unkind way.
Bent the body low to the ground to worship.
Thinking that one is better or greater than others.
Cause problems or suffering for someone.

hotspots.title: The Magicians
hotspots.description: The magicians saw the miracle, bowed down to Allah, and declared their belief.

hotspots.title: The Huge Snake
hotspots.description: Moses’s staff became a huge snake and ate up all the snakes of the magicians.

exercises.title: One Miracle, Different Reactions
exercises.instructions: Match each person or group with their reaction in Chapter 11.
exercises.question: How did each one react when the magicians came to the palace?

matchingPairs.right: bowed down to Allah and declared their belief
still refused to believe because he was arrogant
got frightened at first when the sticks and ropes looked like snakes

correctAnswer.The magicians: bowed down to Allah and declared their belief
correctAnswer.The Pharaoh: still refused to believe because he was arrogant
correctAnswer.Moses (pbuh): got frightened at first when the sticks and ropes looked like snakes

exercises.explanation: When the sticks and ropes looked like snakes, Moses “got frightened”, but Allah told him to throw down his staff. The magicians “bowed down to Allah” and said, “We believe in the Lord of Moses and Harun!” But “The king still refused to believe in Allah because he was arrogant.”

feedback.correct: Well done. The same miracle led the magicians to faith, while pride kept the Pharaoh away from it.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 11 again: The middle tells how Moses felt, and the end tells what the magicians and the king did.

languageFocusExercises.title: Looked Like or Turned Into?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 11. Is the statement true or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: “Once the sticks and ropes fell to the ground, they looked just like snakes!” This sentence tells us that the sticks and ropes really became snakes.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Look (just) like” describes how something seems, not what it really is. The king himself calls it “only magic”. For Moses’s staff, the chapter uses a different verb: it “turned into a huge snake” – a real change. “Once” means “as soon as”: the sticks looked like snakes at the moment they fell.

feedback.correct: Correct. The sticks only seemed to be snakes.
feedback.incorrect: Compare “looked just like snakes” with what happens to Moses’s staff later in Chapter 11.

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about the contest?

errorItems.sentence: The magicians which witnessed this miracle bowed down to Allah.
The Pharaoh did not want to let those who worshipped Allah to live.
He told his advisors and soldiers, “Being rude to them!”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Who” begins a relative clause about people: The magicians who witnessed this miracle. “Let + person + base verb” has no “to”: let them live. An order with “be” uses the base form at the start: “Be rude to them!”

feedback.correct: Well done. You corrected the person clause, the “let” structure and the order.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each sentence with the second half of Chapter 11. Are the magicians people or things? Which verbs are followed by a base verb without “to”?

languageFocusExercises.title: The King Does Not Change
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 11 with words from the bank. Three words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Why did the king still refuse?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: The king [blank] refused to believe in Allah, [blank] he was arrogant. … He continued [blank] Moses (pbuh) and his people day and night.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Still” shows that the refusal continued even after the magicians believed. “Because” + a clause gives the reason (he was arrogant); “because of” would need a noun (because of his arrogance). “Continued to + base verb” shows an action going on over time.

feedback.correct: Correct. You showed continuing refusal, its reason and a continuing action.
feedback.incorrect: The magicians changed, but did the king? Look at what follows each gap: A clause or a verb? Then check the end of Chapter 11.

languageFocusExercises.title: Describe a Turning Point
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about a new idea that most people accept.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who changes their mind, and who does not?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Useful language includes “Once...”, “When...”, a direct imperative, “turned into/became...”, “who...”, “still...”, “continued to...”, and “because...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the five sentences connected around one situation and make the cause of the continued resistance clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give an instruction: “Try …”
discussionPrompts.example: The teacher told the class, “Try the new path before you decide.”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Show the result: “When they …, they …”
discussionPrompts.example: When the students walked along the new path, they reached school ten minutes earlier.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say who changed: “Most of the students …”
discussionPrompts.example: Most of the students saw the result and started to use the new path.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say who did not: “But one boy still …”
discussionPrompts.example: But one boy still took the old road every day.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say why: “He did not change because …”
discussionPrompts.example: He did not change because he did not want to admit that he was wrong.

beforeYouRead.question: Look at the picture. What did Moses’s staff do to the magicians’ snakes?
beforeYouRead.quote: In a second, his staff ate up all the snakes of the magicians.

iCan: I can compare how the magicians and the king reacted.
I can say that something looked like one thing or turned into another.
I can describe a turning point and someone who did not change.

pages.title: The Red Sea
pages.content: Life became harder for them day by day. Moses (pbuh) asked Allah for help. And Allah guided him and told him, “Travel by night with My servants...” Moses (pbuh) called his people and said, “Get ready for the journey. We are going away from Egypt. But you must keep it secret. Nobody should see us. We will leave at night.” They left Egypt at night. They were a large group and among them there were many old people and children. The children and the old could not walk fast and got tired very quickly. That’s why the caravan moved slowly. When the Pharaoh noticed that they had left the land, he prepared his huge army and easily managed to catch up with them. When the sun rose, the caravan reached the Red Sea. Moses (pbuh) and his people saw the king and his soldiers following them. His people panicked. But Moses (pbuh) said, “Calm down! Allah is with us and will show us the way to safety.” Soon, the Pharaoh and his army caught up with them!

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-egypt-ancient
__historical_entity__:moses-red-sea
__historical_entity__:moses-pharaoh
Known only to a few people and hidden from others.
A group of people traveling together.
Reach someone after following them.
Felt sudden strong fear.

hotspots.title: The Night Journey
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) and his people secretly left Egypt at night.

hotspots.title: The Army Behind Them
hotspots.description: The caravan reached the Red Sea while the Pharaoh’s army was catching up with them.

exercises.title: A Slow Caravan
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 12.
exercises.question: Why was the Pharaoh’s army able to catch up with Moses and his people?
options: Someone told the Pharaoh about their secret plan, so he left before them.
They did not leave Egypt until the sun rose, so everyone could see them go.
The caravan moved slowly because the old people and children got tired quickly.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 12 says: “The children and the old could not walk fast and got tired very quickly. That’s why the caravan moved slowly.” They left Egypt “at night”, and the sun rose when they reached the Red Sea.

feedback.correct: Right. Many old people and children could not walk fast, so the whole group was slow.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 12 again. Look for the words “That’s why …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: The Plan and the Rules
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Is it the plan, or an instruction? Put each sentence in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the plan, and what are the rules?

dragDropGroups.group: The plan (what is going to happen)
items: We are going away from Egypt.
We will leave at night.

dragDropGroups.group: Instructions and rules (what people must do or avoid)
items: Get ready for the journey.
But you must keep it secret.
Nobody should see us.

The plan (what is going to happen): We are going away from Egypt.
Instructions and rules (what people must: But you must keep it secret.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Moses uses the present continuous (We are going away) and “will” (We will leave) for a plan that has already been decided. For the rules he uses an imperative (Get ready), “must” for a strong obligation, and “should” for what it is important to avoid.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated the plan from the instructions and rules.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: Does the sentence say what will happen, or what the people must do or avoid? Look for “must”, “should” and a verb with no subject.

languageFocusExercises.title: Cause, Result and Success
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say these lines from Chapter 12?

transformItems.source: The children and the old could not walk fast and got tired very quickly. That’s why the caravan moved slowly.
transformItems.frame: The children and the old could not walk fast and got tired very quickly, [blank] the caravan moved slowly.

transformItems.source: When the Pharaoh noticed that they had left the land, he prepared his huge army and easily managed to catch up with them.
transformItems.frame: … he prepared his huge army and easily succeeded in [blank] up with them.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “That’s why” and “so” both introduce a result. “Could not” shows a past inability, and that inability is the cause. “Manage to + base verb” means succeed in doing something difficult; after “succeed in”, use the -ing form.

feedback.correct: Well done. You joined the cause to its result and expressed success in a new way.
feedback.incorrect: Which short word introduces a result in the middle of a sentence? Which verb form follows a preposition like “in”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Words for the Chase
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word or phrase from Chapter 12 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words tell us about the journey and the chase?

matchingPairs.right: a group of people traveling together
became aware of
reach people who are ahead of you
suddenly became very afraid
Relax and stop worrying!

correctAnswer.caravan: a group of people traveling together
correctAnswer.catch up with: reach people who are ahead of you

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The Pharaoh “noticed” (became aware) that the people had left, and his army could “catch up with” the slow “caravan”. When the people “panicked”, Moses answered with an imperative, “Calm down!”, and a promise with “will”: Allah “will show us the way to safety”.

feedback.correct: Correct. These words carry the chase and the change from panic to calm.
feedback.incorrect: Find each word in Chapter 12 and use the sentence around it to work out its meaning.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain a Difficult Group Plan
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about a group trip with a problem.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the plan, and how does the leader help?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Useful language includes an imperative, “must/should”, “could not”, “That’s why...”, “When...”, “managed to...”, and “will...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the sentences connected around one situation and make the final reassurance respond naturally to the problem.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the plan: “Get ready. We are going to …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our guide said, “Get ready to leave. We are going to walk to the station before the crowds come.”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Give a rule: “You must … / Nobody should …”
discussionPrompts.example: “You must stay together, and nobody should run.”

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give a problem and result: “… could not …. That’s why …”
discussionPrompts.example: My grandparents could not walk fast. That’s why the whole group moved slowly.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say who followed: “When …, they managed to …”
discussionPrompts.example: When another tour group saw us leave, they managed to catch up with us near the station.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Calm the group: “I am with you, and I will …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our guide smiled and said, “I am with you, and I will get you all home safely.”

beforeYouRead.question: Look at the picture. When did Moses (pbuh) and his people leave Egypt?
options: in the middle of the day

iCan: I can tell how Moses (pbuh) and his people left Egypt.
I can explain a plan, its rules and a problem with it.
I can explain a difficult group plan and calm people down.

pages.title: The Cruel King Drowns
pages.content: They were trapped with the Red Sea in front and the king’s army behind them. But Allah was with them. He told Moses (pbuh), “Hit the sea with your stick!” When the stick touched the waters of the sea, a miracle happened! The sea parted! The waves rose high like walls and did not fall down! They could see the sandy ground! Allah made a path for them across the sea! Moses (pbuh) and his people safely walked between the walls of water. The Pharaoh and his soldiers were right behind them. They also saw the road in the middle of the sea. But the Pharaoh turned to his soldiers and said, “Look! The sea opened at my order.” They entered the parted waters and when they were midway, Allah ordered the sea to close. The sea closed over them, and they drowned. The story of Moses (pbuh) has many lessons for us to learn. It again reminds us that no one can enslave another human being. It also shows that the only power over human beings is Allah. Allah sent prophets to show people a better life. They came to teach about Allah and show people right and wrong. Allah is not visible to physical eyes, but He is with us and when we pray to Him, He always guides us on the right path.

exercises.title: The Pharaoh’s Last Words
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the best answer from Chapter 13.
exercises.question: When the Pharaoh saw the path in the sea, he said, “Look! The sea opened at my order.” What does this show about him?
options: He finally believed in the Lord of Moses and Harun at that moment.
He was still too proud to see that only Allah had this power.
He wanted to stop his soldiers from entering the sea after the Israelites.
exercises.explanation: It was Allah who told Moses to hit the sea: “Allah made a path for them across the sea!” But the Pharaoh said it opened “at my order”, and then led his soldiers in. The chapter ends with the lesson that “the only power over human beings is Allah.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Even at the end, his pride made him claim Allah’s miracle for himself.
feedback.incorrect: Compare the Pharaoh’s words with the beginning of Chapter 13: who told Moses to hit the sea, and who made the path?

languageFocusExercises.title: One Moment or Every Time?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the two uses of “when” from Chapter 13. Is the statement true or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: At the end of Chapter 13 we read, “… when we pray to Him, He always guides us on the right path.” Here “when” describes one moment in the story, just like “When the stick touched the waters of the sea”.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: With the present simple and “always”, “when” means “every time”: it states a general truth (when we pray, He guides us). With the past simple, “when” marks one moment in the story that triggers the next event: When the stick touched the water, a miracle happened.

feedback.correct: Correct. The last “when” states a general truth, not one moment in the story.
feedback.incorrect: Compare the tenses: “touched” (past simple) and “pray … guides” (present simple with “always”). Which one is about every time?

languageFocusExercises.title: Through the Sea
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts of Chapter 13 in the right order.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened at the sea, from start to end?

sequencingItems.text: Allah told Moses (pbuh), “Hit the sea with your stick!”
When the stick touched the waters of the sea, a miracle happened!
Allah made a path for Moses and his people across the sea!
Moses (pbuh) and his people safely walked between the walls of water.
The Pharaoh and his army entered the parted waters, and when they were midway, Allah ordered the sea to close.
The sea closed over the Pharaoh and his army, and they drowned.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The command comes first; “When the stick touched …” marks the moment that triggers the miracle. The path is the result, and Moses’s people use it. “When they were midway” marks a second key moment, and “Allah ordered the sea to close” reports an order (order + object + to + base verb). The last sentence gives the final consequence.

feedback.correct: Correct. You followed the command, the two “when” moments and the final consequence.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the command. Moses’s people cross before the Pharaoh’s army enters the water. Check the first paragraph of Chapter 13.

languageFocusExercises.title: From Story to Lesson
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the last lines of Chapter 13. Three words in the bank are extra.
languageFocusExercises.question: What lesson does the story teach?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: The story of Moses (pbuh) has many lessons for us [blank]. It again reminds us [blank] no one can enslave another human being. … Allah sent prophets [blank] show people a better life.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Lessons for us to learn” uses “to + base verb” after a noun to say what we should do with the lessons. “Remind someone that + clause” introduces a general truth drawn from the story. “Sent prophets to show …” uses “to + base verb” for purpose. “For show” is not possible.

feedback.correct: Correct. You moved from the events to the lessons and their purpose.
feedback.incorrect: Look at what follows each gap: A full clause after “reminds us”, and a base verb after the last gap. Check the last paragraph of Chapter 13.

languageFocusExercises.title: From Event to Lesson
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five sentences about an event and the lesson it teaches.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened, and what did you learn?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Useful language includes an imperative, “When...”, a clear result clause, “to + verb” for purpose, and “This reminds us that...” or “This shows that...”.

feedback.correct: Keep one clear situation and make the final lesson grow naturally from the earlier events.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what for: “We used … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: We used big bags to carry the plastic away.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Give the lesson: “This reminds us that …”
discussionPrompts.example: This reminds us that small actions can protect nature.

legend.route:exodus: The night journey to the Red Sea

places.name: Egypt
places.text: Moses (pbuh) was born in the land of Egypt. He lived there in the 13th century BC, over 3000 years ago. At that time, the Pharaoh ruled Egypt, and the Children of Israel were a large group there. Moses grew up safely in the palace of the Pharaoh.
places.teacherNote: The B1 text does not say where the palace or the city was, so Egypt is shown as a region, not as one exact place.
places.question: Why was the Pharaoh afraid of the Children of Israel?

places.name: The River Nile
places.text: Moses’s mother put her baby in a basket and took it to the River Nile. The waters carried the basket away, and the waves brought it ashore near the Pharaoh’s palace. When Queen Asiye saw the baby, she felt a strong love for him.
places.teacherNote: The text does not say where on the Nile this happened. The soft area only shows the river in Egypt.
places.question: Why did Moses’s mother put her baby in the river?

places.name: Midian
places.text: Moses escaped from Egypt and, after many days, he reached the land of Midian. It was the closest place between Egypt and Syria, on the eastern side of the Gulf of Aqaba, and the Pharaoh was not the ruler there. At a well, Moses helped two sisters. Then he lived in Midian for about ten years.
places.teacherNote: In chapter 6 the English text says Midian was “the closest place between Egypt and Syria”; the Arabic text says it was near the road between Egypt and al-Sham. The exact place of the well is not known.
places.question: How did Moses help the two sisters? What happened after that?

places.name: The Mountain
places.text: After about ten years, Moses and his family started to travel towards Egypt. It was winter. While they were crossing a valley between mountains, Moses saw a fire on the hillside. He climbed the mountain and heard the voice of Allah.
places.teacherNote: The B1 text does not name this mountain. The B2 book calls it Mount Sinai, also known as Mount Tur. The soft area in the south of the Sinai Peninsula is approximate; the exact place is not known.
places.question: Which two signs did Allah give Moses on the mountain?

places.name: The Red Sea
places.text: Moses (pbuh) and his people left Egypt at night. When the sun rose, the caravan reached the Red Sea, and the Pharaoh’s army was behind them. Allah parted the sea, so they walked safely between the walls of water. Then the sea closed over the Pharaoh and his soldiers, and they drowned.
places.teacherNote: The exact place of the crossing is not known. The soft area near the Gulf of Suez, in the north of the Red Sea, is approximate.
places.question: How did Moses’s people feel when they saw the army? What did Moses say to them?

pages.title: Knowledge Check
pages.content: Test your understanding of the B1 story of Prophet Moses (pbuh).

exercises.title: A Mother’s Fear
exercises.instructions: Choose the best answer. Use the evidence in Chapter 2.
exercises.question: Moses’s mother was so frightened that she could not sleep. What exactly was she afraid of?
options: that the soldiers could hear baby Moses crying
that the Pharaoh would take her to the palace
that the river would carry her baby too far
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “His mother was so frightened that she was unable to sleep at night. She was scared that when Moses cried, the soldiers could hear his voice.”

feedback.correct: Correct. The soldiers were searching houses for baby boys, so even a baby’s cry could put Moses in danger.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Reread the end of Chapter 2, just after “Moses (pbuh) was born in that year”. Why was she scared when he cried?

exercises.title: Close to the Israelites
exercises.instructions: Choose the best answer. Use the evidence in Chapter 4.
exercises.question: Moses grew up in the Pharaoh’s palace. Why did he still feel close to the Children of Israel?
options: The Pharaoh sent him to live with them for a time.
He had worked with them in the fields as a boy.
His mother was one of the Children of Israel.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “Young Moses felt close to the Children of Israel because he was originally not from a family of the palace and his mother was one of the Children of Israel.”

feedback.correct: Correct. He lived in the palace, but his roots were with the Children of Israel through his mother.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Reread the last sentence of Chapter 4. What two reasons does it give?

exercises.title: Queen Asiye
exercises.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the story.
exercises.question: According to Chapter 4, people always remember Queen Asiye because of her goodness and courage.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “Queen Asiye also took care of Moses and raised him in the palace with love. People always remember her because of her goodness and courage.”

feedback.correct: Right, the statement is true. She raised Moses with love in the palace of a cruel king, and people remember her goodness and courage.
feedback.incorrect: Reread the middle of Chapter 4, after Moses returns to his mother. Why do people remember Queen Asiye?

exercises.title: The Next Day
exercises.instructions: Choose the best answer. Use the evidence in Chapter 5.
exercises.question: The same Israelite called Moses for help again the next day. What did Moses understand about him?
options: He was a quarrelsome man, not a peaceable one.
He was the Pharaoh’s spy in the busy bazaar.
He was weak and needed Moses’s help every day.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “The man once more called out to Moses, “Help me!” Moses understood that the Israelite was a quarrelsome man, not a peaceable man.”

feedback.correct: Correct. A second fight with the same man showed Moses that this man often started quarrels.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Reread the second paragraph of Chapter 5. What did Moses understand when the man called him again?

exercises.title: The Sisters at the Well
exercises.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the story.
exercises.question: Shu’ayb (pbuh) sent his daughters to the well alone because he was very old.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “Prophet Shu’ayb (pbuh) was very old. That’s why he had to send the girls alone.” The girls also said, “Our father is very old. He cannot come with us.”

feedback.correct: Right, the statement is true. He was very old and could not go with them himself.
feedback.incorrect: Reread the end of Chapter 7 and what the girls said at the start. Why did their father not come with them?

exercises.title: The Shining Hand
exercises.instructions: Choose the best answer. Use the evidence in Chapter 9.
exercises.question: Moses took his hand out of his chest. What did Allah say about it?
options: It would stay white for the rest of his life.
It was shining like silver but was not harmed.
It would give him the strength to fight.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 9: “Put your hand into your chest. Now take it out. See, your hand is now shining like silver. But it is not harmed.”

feedback.correct: Correct. The hand was changed as a sign of Allah’s power, but Moses himself was not hurt.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Reread Allah’s words about the hand in the first paragraph of Chapter 9. What does the sentence after “shining like silver” say?

exercises.title: Going to the Palace
exercises.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the story.
exercises.question: Moses took his brother Harun with him when he went to the Pharaoh’s palace.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 10: “Allah chose Moses (pbuh) to be His prophet. Moses (pbuh) took his brother Harun (pbuh) with him as his companion and went to the palace.”

feedback.correct: Right, the statement is true. Moses took his brother Harun with him as his companion.
feedback.incorrect: Reread the first lines of Chapter 10. Who went to the palace with Moses?

exercises.title: The Last Lesson
exercises.instructions: Choose the best answer. Use the evidence in Chapter 13.
exercises.question: According to the last lines of the story, what happens when we pray to Allah?
options: He shows Himself to our eyes.
He guides us on the right path.
He gives us power over other people.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 13: “Allah is not visible to physical eyes, but He is with us and when we pray to Him, He always guides us on the right path.”

feedback.correct: Correct. The story ends with this promise: Allah cannot be seen, but He is with us and guides us when we pray.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Reread the last sentence of Chapter 13. Can Allah be seen, and what does He do when we pray?

exercises.title: Notice: Make, Let, Tell and Order
exercises.instructions: Look at the verb after the person. Put each sentence in the right group.
exercises.question: After make, let, tell and order + a person: “to” or no “to”?

items: He made the Children of Israel do dangerous work for little or no money.
The Pharaoh did not want to let those who worshipped Allah live.
Let me go and take some burning sticks from the fire …
Moses’s mother was very worried and told her daughter to follow the basket.
Allah told the waves to be kind while carrying the baby.
… Allah ordered the sea to close.

verb + person + base verb (no “to”): He made the Children of Israel do dangerous work for little or no money.
The Pharaoh did not want to let those who worshipped Allah live.
Let me go and take some burning sticks from the fire …
verb + person + “to” + verb: Moses’s mother was very worried and told her daughter to follow the basket.
Allah told the waves to be kind while carrying the baby.
… Allah ordered the sea to close.

exercises.explanation: “Make” and “let” are followed by a person and the base verb, with no “to”: made the Children of Israel do, let those who worshipped Allah live, let me go. “Tell” and “order” are followed by a person and “to” + verb: told her daughter to follow, told the waves to be kind, ordered the sea to close. This is also the way we report an order without quoting it. In the passive, “to” comes back after make: The Children of Israel were made to do dangerous work.

feedback.correct: Well done. Make and let take the base verb; tell and order take “to” + verb.
feedback.incorrect: Find the verb just after the person (the Children of Israel, those, me, her daughter, the waves, the sea). Is there a “to” before it?

It is important that this does not happen.
correctAnswer.Moses (pbuh) had no choice but to displa: Only one action was still possible.

exercises.explanation: “Have to” shows necessity. “Did not have to” means that it was not necessary; it does not mean “not allowed”. “Cannot” shows that someone is not able to do something. “Should” (here with “nobody”) shows what is important to do or to avoid. “Have no choice but to + verb” means that the other ways have failed, so only one action is left.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated necessity, no need, inability, advice and the only possible action.
feedback.incorrect: Ask for each line: Is it necessary, not necessary, not possible, important to avoid, or the only way left? Check Chapters 7, 10 and 12.

exercises.title: Notice: Setting the Scene
exercises.instructions: Read the two scenes. Then choose the best answer.
exercises.question: Chapter 6: “Moses was tired and thirsty. He was looking for water. Soon, he found a well …” Chapter 10: “The king was sitting on his throne, and his advisors and soldiers were standing around him. Moses (pbuh) told him about Allah.” What do “was looking”, “was sitting” and “were standing” do in these scenes?
options: They show actions that started after the main event, when Moses found the well or spoke to the king.
They describe the situation that was already in progress when the main event happened.
They show things that happened every day for many years in Madyan and in the palace.
They show what the people were planning to do next, after Moses had left them.
exercises.explanation: The past continuous (was/were + -ing) paints the background: An action already in progress. The past simple then tells the main event that happens in that scene: He found a well; Moses told him about Allah. The same contrast opens Chapter 5: while Moses was walking in the bazaar, he saw two men fighting.

feedback.correct: Correct. Was/were + -ing sets the scene; the past simple moves the story on.
feedback.incorrect: Which action was already going on, and which one happened at one moment inside that scene? Look again at Chapters 6 and 10.

exercises.title: Build: Contrast, Reason, Purpose, Result
exercises.instructions: Complete the lines from the book with words from the bank. Two words are not needed.
exercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
exercises.fillBlanksText: They also had sheep with them. [blank] they did not go near it. … He accepted the offer, [blank] he was a stranger in Midian and he urgently needed a job and a house. … Allah gave them to Moses (pbuh) [blank] help him against the Pharaoh. … The children and the old could not walk fast and got tired very quickly. [blank] the caravan moved slowly.
exercises.explanation: “But” shows a contrast: The girls had sheep, and yet they stayed away from the water. “Because” + a clause (subject + verb) gives the reason for accepting the job. “In order to” + base verb gives the purpose of the miracles. “That’s why” starts a new sentence with the result of the slow walking. “Because of” needs a noun, not a clause, and “so that” needs a subject and a verb after it.

feedback.correct: Well done. You linked contrast, reason, purpose and result.
feedback.incorrect: For each gap, ask: Is the next part a contrast, a reason, a purpose or a result? Then check what follows the gap: A clause, a base verb or a new sentence.

exercises.title: Build: “To” + Verb or -ing?
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from the book.
exercises.question: After keep, manage and decide: “to” + verb or -ing?

formChoices.sentence: The Pharaoh kept [choice] to believe in Allah.
When the Pharaoh noticed that they had left the land, he prepared his huge army and easily managed [choice] up with them.
After living in Midian for about ten years, … Moses decided [choice] back to Egypt.

exercises.explanation: “Keep” is followed by -ing: Kept refusing shows that the refusal happened again and again (Chapter 10). “Manage” and “decide” are followed by “to” + verb: managed to catch up means that the army succeeded (Chapter 12), and decided to go back is a choice about the future (Chapter 8). “Continue” can take both: continued to rule, continued to trouble.

feedback.correct: Correct. Keep + -ing; manage and decide + “to” + verb.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verb before the gap: kept, managed or decided. Which one needs -ing, and which ones need “to”? Check Chapters 8, 10 and 12.

exercises.title: Build: Who, Where and Until
exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
exercises.question: Can you fix who, where and until?

errorItems.sentence: The queen, which was different from her husband, was good, kind-hearted, and believed in Allah.
The next day, Moses was again in the bazaar which he saw two men fighting.
We have to be patient until the other shepherds will go away.

exercises.explanation: “Who” begins a clause about a person: The queen, who was different from her husband (Chapter 3). “Where” begins a clause about a place: The bazaar where he saw two men fighting (Chapter 5). After a time word like “until”, we use the present simple for the future, not “will”: until the other shepherds go away (Chapter 7).

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed the person clause, the place clause and the time clause.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: Is the clause about a person, a place or a time? Compare with Chapters 3, 5 and 7.

exercises.title: Build: Report the Words
exercises.instructions: Report what the people said. Write the missing words.
exercises.question: What changes when we report someone’s words?

transformItems.source: She said to her servants, “Find a nurse for the baby.”
transformItems.frame: She told her servants [blank] a nurse for the baby.
Moses (pbuh) told his people that they [blank] at night.

transformItems.source: Moses asked the girls, “Why are you sitting far away from the spring?”
transformItems.frame: Moses asked the girls why they [blank] far away from the spring.

exercises.explanation: A reported order uses tell + person + “to” + verb: “Find …” becomes told her servants to find. A reported plan moves back in time: “will leave” becomes would leave, as in Chapter 1, where the Pharaoh feared that the group would take control. A reported question keeps the normal order, subject before verb, and moves back in time: “Why are you sitting …?” becomes why they were sitting. The pronouns change too: we → they, you → they.

feedback.correct: Well done. You reported an order, a plan and a question.
feedback.incorrect: Check three things: tell + person + “to”; will → would; and in a reported question, subject + verb (they were …), with no question mark.

exercises.title: Use: Getting Ready for the School Fair
exercises.instructions: Complete this new text with words from the bank. Three words are extra.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s words in a school story?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Last Friday, our class was preparing a stand for the school fair. Some students were painting a big sign, and others were carrying tables into the garden. Our teacher, Mrs Demir, told us to finish everything before three o’clock. Deniz, [blank] had a broken arm, could not carry anything heavy. [blank] she wrote the price cards in beautiful letters. Everyone helped, and we managed [blank] the stand at half past two. We did not [blank] ask the older students for help. At the end of the day, Mrs Demir let us choose a name for our stand.
exercises.explanation: “Who” adds information about a person (Deniz). “That’s why” gives the result of her broken arm. “Manage” takes “to” + verb: managed to open. “Did not have to” means that there was no need to ask for help. The text also uses the past continuous for the background (was preparing, were painting), told us to finish and let us choose.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s language in a new situation.
feedback.incorrect: Ask for each gap: A person? a result? which form after “managed”? necessary or not necessary?

exercises.title: Use: Check a Friend’s Sentences
exercises.instructions: Each sentence from a classmate has one mistake. Tap it and choose the correct words.
exercises.question: Can you help your classmate fix the sentences?

errorItems.sentence: My grandmother made me to promise that I would call her every week.
While I was walking to school, I was seeing an old man fall on the ice.
Our coach told us that the bus will leave at eight, so we had to get up early.

exercises.explanation: “Make + person + base verb” has no “to”: made me promise. The past continuous gives the background (was walking), and the past simple gives the short event that happened in the middle of it (I saw); “see” is not normally used in the continuous with this meaning. In a report about the past, “will” moves back to “would”: told us that the bus would leave.

feedback.correct: Well done. You corrected all three sentences.
feedback.incorrect: Think of the book: Made the Children of Israel do; while Moses was walking, he saw; feared that this group would take control.

exercises.title: Use: A Plan That Needed Help
exercises.instructions: Write 5–6 sentences about a hard job you did with others. Tell a partner first.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s language to tell your own story?
exercises.explanation: Example: “Last spring, our class was planning a trip to the science museum. While we were collecting the money, our teacher told us to bring our own lunch. Two students could not pay for the bus, so we had a cake sale in order to help them. That’s why everyone was able to come. We managed to reach the museum on time, and we did not have to wait in the long queue. Our teacher let us choose the last activity of the day.”

feedback.correct: Check your sentences: was/were + -ing for the background, have to / did not have to / could not, because / so / that’s why / in order to, told us to …, let us …, managed to …

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Set the scene: “Last …, we were …ing when …”
discussionPrompts.example: Last spring, we were preparing for our school fair when heavy rain started.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what you had to do: “We had to … / We could not …”
discussionPrompts.example: We had to move all the tables inside, but we could not carry the big tent alone.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give reasons: “because … . That’s why … . We … in order to …”
discussionPrompts.example: The tent was very heavy because it was wet. That’s why we asked the parents for help. We worked together in order to finish before the guests arrived.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say how it ended: “Our teacher told us to … . In the end, we managed to …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our teacher told us to put the tables in the hall and let us use the music room too. In the end, we managed to open the fair on time.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Test your knowledge of the entire B1 story of Prophet Moses (pbuh).

exercises.title: Two Versions of a Dream
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that connects the two chapters.
exercises.question: Chapters 1 and 2 both describe the Pharaoh’s dream. What do the two versions have in common?
options: The danger comes from the Children of Israel.
A great fire burns down the Pharaoh’s palace.
The Egyptians leave the land of Egypt forever.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “In his vision, he saw an Israelite take him down from his throne.” Chapter 2: “The fire came from Jerusalem and burnt the houses of the Egyptians, but did not do any harm to the Children of Israel.”

feedback.correct: Yes. In both versions, the Pharaoh’s power is in danger and the Children of Israel are safe.
feedback.incorrect: Compare the last sentence of Chapter 1 with the words of Ibn Abbas in Chapter 2. Who is in danger, and who is not?

exercises.title: Allah’s Promise
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 3 with one word: shelter, palace or sea.
exercises.question: What did Allah promise Moses’s mother about the basket?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Waters will carry it to the [blank].
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3 begins: “Put your baby in the basket. Take the basket to the River Nile. Waters will carry it to the shelter.” Later, the waves bring the basket “ashore near the Pharaoh’s palace”, and the baby is safe there.

feedback.correct: Yes. A “shelter” is a safe place, and Allah kept His promise.
feedback.incorrect: Read Allah’s words at the start of Chapter 3. Where will the waters carry the basket?

exercises.title: Moses’s Words
exercises.instructions: Match each of Moses’s sayings with the moment when he said it.
exercises.question: When did Moses say these words?

matchingPairs.left: “Forgive me! I didn’t do it on purpose.”
matchingPairs.right: after the fight in the bazaar

matchingPairs.left: “Why are you sitting far away from the spring?”
matchingPairs.right: at the well in Midian

matchingPairs.left: “Wait here. Let me go and take some burning sticks from the fire to get warm.”
matchingPairs.right: on the winter journey back to Egypt

matchingPairs.left: “Calm down! Allah is with us and will show us the way to safety.”
matchingPairs.right: at the Red Sea, with the army behind them

correctAnswer.“Forgive me! I didn’t do it on purpose.”: after the fight in the bazaar
correctAnswer.“Wait here. Let me go and take some burn: on the winter journey back to Egypt
correctAnswer.“Calm down! Allah is with us and will sh: at the Red Sea, with the army behind them

exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: Moses prays after the Egyptian’s death. Chapter 6: he speaks to the two girls at the well. Chapter 8: “It was winter.” He sees a fire and speaks to his family. Chapter 12: “His people panicked.” Moses calms them.

feedback.correct: Yes. Each saying fits its moment: a prayer, a question, a plan and words of trust.
feedback.incorrect: Think about where Moses is in each saying: In the city, at a well, in a cold valley or by the sea.

exercises.title: Waiting at the Spring
exercises.instructions: Choose the best explanation.
exercises.question: The sisters say: “We have to be patient until the other shepherds go away.” What does this mean?
options: They were not allowed to use the spring at all.
They were waiting for their father to arrive.
They watered their sheep only after the men left.
exercises.explanation: In Chapter 7 the sisters explain: “There are no young men in our house to help us with the animals. So, we have to take the sheep to the water ourselves. We have to wait our turn. We have to be patient until the other shepherds go away.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Without help, they always had to be the last at the water.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sisters’ words at the start of Chapter 7. When could they take their sheep to the water?

exercises.title: Heartless Soldiers
exercises.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
exercises.question: The Pharaoh’s soldiers showed no pity to the crying families.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2 says: “All mothers, fathers and sisters cried, but the soldiers who were heartless showed no pity.”

feedback.correct: True. The story calls them “heartless”: the families’ tears did not change them.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2. How did the soldiers act when the families cried?

exercises.title: Places in the Story
exercises.instructions: Match each place with what happened there.
exercises.question: What happened in each of these places?

matchingPairs.right: The waves brought the basket ashore.
Moses hit an Egyptian, who died by accident.
Moses heard a voice in the silence.
The magicians bowed down to Allah.

correctAnswer.the River Nile: The waves brought the basket ashore.
correctAnswer.the bazaar: Moses hit an Egyptian, who died by accident.
correctAnswer.the mountain: Moses heard a voice in the silence.
correctAnswer.the palace: The magicians bowed down to Allah.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “Soon, the waves brought the basket ashore near the Pharaoh’s palace.” Chapter 5: “He hit the Egyptian and accidentally caused someone’s death.” Chapter 9: “In the silence he heard a thundering voice”. Chapter 11: “The magicians who witnessed this miracle bowed down to Allah.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Each place marks a turning point in Moses’s life.
feedback.incorrect: Look again at Chapters 3, 5, 9 and 11.

exercises.title: A Secret Plan
exercises.instructions: Choose the reason the story gives.
exercises.question: Why did Moses tell his people, “But you must keep it secret.”?
options: so that the old people could rest
so that nobody would see them leave
so that the army would wait for them
exercises.explanation: In Chapter 12 Moses says: “But you must keep it secret. Nobody should see us. We will leave at night.” The Pharaoh followed only “When the Pharaoh noticed that they had left the land”.

feedback.correct: Yes. Leaving in secret gave them time before the Pharaoh noticed.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentence after “keep it secret” in Chapter 12.

exercises.title: Walls of Water
exercises.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
exercises.question: When the stick touched the sea, the water rose like walls, but the walls fell down at once.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 13 says: “The waves rose high like walls and did not fall down! They could see the sandy ground!”

feedback.correct: Right. The walls stayed up until Moses and his people were safe.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 13 again. What did the walls of water do?

exercises.title: Free People
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 13 with one word: enslave, forgive or help.
exercises.question: What lesson does the story of Moses remind us of?
exercises.fillBlanksText: It again reminds us that no one can [blank] another human being.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 13 says: “It again reminds us that no one can enslave another human being. It also shows that the only power over human beings is Allah.”

feedback.correct: Yes. The Pharaoh treated the Children of Israel like slaves, but the story says no one has that right.
feedback.incorrect: Read the lessons at the end of Chapter 13. Think about how the Pharaoh treated the Children of Israel.

exercises.title: Moses’s Journey
exercises.instructions: Put these events in the order of the story.
exercises.question: How does the story move from the Pharaoh’s dream to the Red Sea?

sequencingItems.text: Moses marries one of Shu’ayb’s daughters.
The Pharaoh’s advisors explain his dream.
The Pharaoh says that the sea opened at his order.
A man from the city tells Moses to run away.
Moses takes his brother Harun to the palace.
Queen Asiye tells her servants to find a nurse.

exercises.explanation: The dream (Chapter 2), the nurse (Chapter 4), the escape (Chapter 6), the marriage in Midian (Chapter 8), Harun and Moses at the palace (Chapter 10) and the Red Sea (Chapter 13).

feedback.correct: Yes. The story follows Moses from the palace to Midian and back to the Pharaoh.
feedback.incorrect: Remember that Moses met Shu’ayb’s family only after he ran away from Egypt.
